definition: A breakdown pose's TIME position, chosen by estimating when a specific physical event will occur (e.g. the instant a jumping character's knees will be fully straightened, or a landing's deepest compression), becomes the anchor a combined ease-out-in is built from - replacing the arithmetic midpoint between the two flanking key poses, so a bisection-based inbetweening method (the halves method) allocates a different number of frames to each side depending on where that estimated moment falls.
purpose: Explain WHERE within a phase to place a breakdown's frame, and why that choice - not the geometric middle - determines how many inbetween frames should fall on each side of it.
visible_effect: The inbetweens on one side of the breakdown are visibly denser (more frames, a slower build) than the other side, in proportion to how far the breakdown's estimated frame sits from the span's arithmetic middle - rather than a symmetric ease-out-in with matched frame counts on each side.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: Lets a specific anatomical or physical event (legs fully straightening before liftoff, a landing's deepest compression) land on its own readable frame instead of being smeared across a generic symmetric ease, and lets the surrounding spacing honestly reflect how much of the phase happens before versus after that event.
physical_interpretation: A breakdown placed by physical estimation stands in for an unmeasured real-world event - the animator's best guess at when a joint reaches a particular configuration - used as a hard constraint the surrounding spacing must then respect, a lower-rigor sibling of grounding a phase's timing in an actual stopwatch or filmed measurement.
use_cases: a transition where two flanking key poses cannot be interpolated directly into each other without passing through an intermediate, physically-necessary configuration (the video's own case: interpolating straight from a bent-knee anticipation crouch to a bent-knee action pose skips the moment the knees are actually straight, which is physically what has to happen for a real leg to generate upward force)
deciding, once a breakdown's frame is chosen, how many of the phase's available inbetween frames should go on each side of it, rather than splitting them evenly by default
non_use_cases: a transition where the two flanking poses ARE directly interpolable with no missing intermediate configuration - inserting a breakdown here only adds authoring work for no visible benefit

a phase where the actual timing of the physical event is known precisely (measured by stopwatch or filmed timecode, per `physical_reference_timing_method`) rather than estimated - the estimation method this entry describes is the fallback when no such measurement exists, not a replacement for one
interactions: `ai/plan.js authorMotion`'s breakdown step (`AUTHOR_STEP_KINDS`) already computes a breakdown as a POSE BIAS at a declared frame `bd.at` - this entry is real-world evidence for how a professional animator actually chooses that `at` value (physical-event estimation) and for why it is deliberately NOT the span's time midpoint, matching the source code comment ('A breakdown is a POSE BIAS, not a time fraction') from the opposite direction: this video shows the TIME placement also departing from the midpoint, on top of the POSE value already documented as doing so

physical_reference_timing_method (W01, video 9) - the measured, higher-rigor sibling of this technique: that card grounds timing in a stopwatch reading or a filmed timecode, while this entry's placement is explicitly an estimate ('let's estimate... it's probably here') with no measurement behind it

spacing_subdivision_method_ladder (W02, video 11) - this entry names WHERE the ladder's halves method should be anchored from when a breakdown is present, which that card's own halves/thirds/favors description does not address
cadence_representation: Partially represented, with a genuine gap: `authorMotion` already accepts a breakdown's frame (`bd.at`) as an arbitrary caller-supplied number and computes its POSE from a declared `bias`, but nothing in `ai/plan.js` derives or suggests an `at` value from a physical-event estimate the way this video's presenter does by eye - a caller must already know or guess the frame before calling `authorMotion`, the same 'this compiler will not invent durations' boundary the module's own header comment states for phase timing generally.
control_surface: `authorMotion`'s `phases[].breakdown.at` (frame) and `.bias` (pose fraction) together are the existing surface; no tool derives `at` from anything resembling a physical-event estimate.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Not measurable as stated - 'when the knees will be fully straightened' is a property of a physical performance this build has no access to, not of project data. What IS measurable, given an already-authored breakdown, is whether the resulting inbetween DENSITY is in fact asymmetric across it (`key_density` per side, already computed by `ai/motion.js`), which would at least confirm the redistribution effect even though it cannot verify the estimate itself was physically correct.
generation_or_modification_methods: None - `authorMotion` compiles a breakdown already supplied with `at` and `bias`; nothing generates either value from an estimate or a measurement.
failure_modes: anchoring the ease-out-in split at the phase's arithmetic middle by default when a breakdown is present, producing the exact 'knees stay bent throughout' problem the video shows and then corrects
an estimate placed with too little care, landing the breakdown's frame far enough from the true physical event that the surrounding spacing still looks arbitrary rather than motivated
roblox_considerations: None beyond the general keyframe/easing model; Roblox's Animation Editor has no notion of a physically-estimated breakdown either - the estimation step happens in the animator's judgment before any keys are placed, on either platform.
examples: the anticipation-to-action breakdown: 'let's estimate when that last point of contact would happen, it's probably here where we'll have the knees straighten up' - placed such that the resulting ease-out from anticipation needed only one inbetween while the ease-in to action kept the rest (video @ 09:27-10:11)

the action-to-overshoot breakdown, placed 'at the end, and not the middle' specifically because the phase's physics call for a pure easing-out (continuous acceleration under gravity, no possible deceleration partway) rather than a symmetric easing out-in (video @ 10:50-11:58)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/n29cFugfM_c @ 09:27-11:58 - Plainly Simple states the estimation reasoning and its effect on frame distribution directly and explicitly in the transcript for both the anticipation-to-action and action-to-overshoot transitions; this session's own focused re-extraction at t=08:27-08:30 directly shows the real-footage crouch-then-explosive-extension reference consistent with the presenter's estimate; cross-checked against `ai/plan.js AUTHOR_STEP_KINDS`/breakdown-bias implementation read directly from source in this session; experimental until validated
